newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG TAKES OVERALL LEAD WITH SLALOM WIN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG TAKES OVERALL LEAD WITH SLALOM WIN.

text.p: Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg fulfilled her goals of finishing ahead of favourite Claudia Riegler in a slalom and snatching the lead in the overall World Cup standings by scoring her second World Cup success of the season on Saturday.

The Austrian-born Riegler, who races for her mother's country New Zealand after disagreeing with her native ski federation, had won both previous slaloms this season, in Park City, Utah, and Crans Montana.
Riegler was third in the 58-gate first leg but was poor on the second run through 59 gates to fall back to ninth overall.
Wiberg, second to Riegler in both previous slaloms, clocked fastest times in both runs for a total of one minute 42.76 seconds and victory by more than a full second.
The Olympic and world champion overtook Germany's defending overall winner Katja Seizinger in the standings. Seizinger, who decided to miss the weekend's races, is now 68 points behind the Swede.
"Today I was the lucky one. I managed two good runs and bib number one again brought me luck," said Wiberg, who also won the first of two slaloms in Semmering last year with the same start number.
A disappointed Riegler said after the race on the Hirschenkogel piste: "It was not my day. I couldn't find my rhythm. But I will try my luck in tomorrow's slalom. I like this slope."
Italian Deborah Compagnoni improved on a first leg sixth place to post a total time of 1:43.88 for second place.
Austria's 1993 World Cup champion Anita Wachter delighted home crowds of 10,000 at the small resort some 70 kms southwest of Vienna by earning the third podium position in 1:43.94.
But the day belonged to Wiberg, a 26-year-old allrounder who also won the Super-g at Lake Louise in November and now has 15 career victories.

The Swede, who has had her sights firmly set on the coveted overall title for the past few years, remained realistic on Saturday and said: "It is too early to think about the overalls. I will only start thinking about it after the world championships (in Sestriere in February)."
"I would like to make a medal in either downhill or super-g," said Wiberg, who took world championship giant slalom gold in 1991 and combined gold last February in Sierra Nevada.
"I would also really like to win the overall titles in slalom and downhill this season. That is what I am concentrating on at the moment."

Wiberg, who took a three-day break over Christmas to celebrate with her parents in Sweden, also hopes to do well in Sunday's second slalom on the same slope: "Another victory tomorrow would be great. The slope is in perfect condition -- hard and a bit icy -- so it should be a good race."
Compagnoni, who is still chasing a maiden slalom win, was content with second place.
"I was really disappointed after failing to finish at Crans Montana. I told myself I had to be less aggressive here and it worked. I really wanted to finish," she said.
Wachter, whose best result this winter was a second place in a giant slalom at Park City, scored her best slalom result in three years.

"I am surprised with this result because I did not train much slalom over the summer. But the crowds inspired me today. It's always great to race in front of a home crowd," said Wachter, a 29-year-old veteran who has been a regular on the circuit since 1985.
Another Austrian, Elfi Eder, winner of last winter's overall slalom title, recorded her best result of the season by finishing fourth in 1:44.50. Sweden's Ylva Nowen was fifth in 1:44.57.
